Oral medicine and dentistry · published research

Graft-versus-host disease

Uncontrolled reports describe oral pain or lesion improvement, including immediate pain reductions across treatment sessions. There are no controlled trials, and some publications reuse earlier cases.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Uncontrolled reports describe oral pain or lesion improvement, including immediate pain reductions across treatment sessions. There are no controlled trials, and some publications reuse earlier cases.

Summary of the Evidence

The category contains eight records: one review and seven human clinical publications, mostly case reports or case series, plus one retrospective study. Epstein et al.'s 2020 maintenance report continues the seven cases published in 2017 and is not an independent cohort; some case reports also combine PBM with photodynamic therapy. No animal or in-vitro/ex-vivo study is listed.

Human and clinical evidence

In a retrospective series of 11 patients, pain fell immediately after most treatment sessions; small case series describe improvement in oral sensitivity, mucosal lesions or fibrosis (Finfter et al. 2021; Epstein et al., 2017, 2020). Acute case reports describe healing over several days, but uncontrolled designs, concomitant care and repeated reports prevent causal conclusions. Clinical presentations range from ulcer pain to fibrosis, and the reports use different schedules and outcomes. Immediate analgesia after a session, lesion healing over days, and longer-term fibrotic change should not be combined as one endpoint. Controlled studies would need stable background immunosuppression, prespecified oral outcomes, and longer surveillance for durability and safety.

Primary original study: Finfter et al. 2021 overlapping maintenance report: Epstein et al. 2020

Animal evidence

none identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Finfter et al. report a 940 nm diode laser, pulsed at a 50 percent duty cycle and 0.7 W, with 90 seconds per lesion point. This is near-infrared light, outside the visible band. Other GVHD case reports use differing approaches and background care, so this schedule is not a common protocol across the literature.

Interpretation

Immediate pain relief, lesion healing, and longer-term fibrosis are distinct outcomes. Case reports and repeated publications can overstate the number of independent patients if titles are counted as cohorts. Controlled studies would need to account for background immunosuppression and assess durability and adverse events.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. Uncontrolled reports overlap, and no controlled clinical trial is listed.
Publications and records8 unique titles.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The evidence comprises case reports, case series, one retrospective study, and a review. The 2020 maintenance publication follows the same seven patients reported in 2017, rather than adding an independent cohort. A retrospective series reports immediate session-level pain changes, but the absence of controlled comparisons prevents causal conclusions.
